stem.en: A drop of ink takes ten minutes to spread through a glass 5 cm across. Kabir says it will take twenty minutes for a glass 10 cm across. What does the random walk say?

text.en: About forty minutes. A walker needs four times the steps to go twice the distance.

feedback.en: That is true for a walker in a straight line. A random walker doubles back constantly, and twice the distance costs four times the steps.
Ink has no speed of its own. It has a step rate, and distance covered grows only with the square root of the steps.

text.en: It never spreads through a bigger glass.

feedback.en: It always spreads. It just takes longer, and more than proportionally.

explanation.en: Distance grows with the square root of steps. Doubling distance means four times the steps, so four times the time.
